main.summary:
Backend engineer designing and operating a shared backend platform across 6 live game environments (12 branches), and leading the newly formed Platform Part to build team-wide AI development infrastructure. At GameDuo, drove an 82% BigQuery cost reduction, a 270x throughput expansion via serverless migration, and a WAL-sharded real-time game chat server (6,000 CCU target); presented the case study at Games on AWS 2025.

Over {{CAREER_DURATION}} across four domains (Education, Healthcare, Clinical Trials, Gaming), consistently delivered DB optimization, concurrency control, and event-driven architecture design. Since late 2024, I have applied this same structural thinking to the development process itself — orchestrating multiple AI agents by role to design and ship production software. Right after the new Part launched, I designed and shipped GameDuo Platform Harness — a shared AI context infrastructure that converts individual learnings into reusable team assets.

items: Query tuning, index design, and table normalization delivering 97% performance gain
Deadlock root cause analysis and distributed locking — diagnosing and resolving data-layer bottlenecks
Sharded a Redis Streams WAL across a 4-shard cluster for real-time chat message ordering and horizontal scaling (accept rate 99.39→99.99%, ack p95 767ms→6.6ms)
Batch-to-EDA migration expanding throughput 270x, Lambda hybrid pipeline design
BigQuery pricing model analysis with read-method switch — 82% cost reduction
Express monolith to NestJS via 3-stage progressive migration, TDD-driven incident-free deployments during major releases
Shared package system unifying 7 projects, cutting deployment from 3h to 15min
Integrated Claude Code, Amazon Q, and other AI agents into development workflows, driving team-wide adoption (Games on AWS 2025 speaker)
Established team-wide TDD foundation to ensure AI-generated code reliability — built a quality governance layer for AI-assisted development

Query optimization, deadlock root cause analysis, large-scale table normalization, Redis distributed locking

projects.name: Real-Time Game Chat Server (Multi-Tenant)
projects.description: Designed a multi-tenant real-time chat server shared across live games, validating a 6,000 CCU / 18,000 RPS capacity target through load testing
projects.techRationale: Adopted a Redis Streams-based WAL (Write-Ahead Log) for message ordering, and distributed it across a 4-shard Valkey cluster instead of vertical scaling — a single-threaded Redis cannot resolve write bottlenecks by adding cores. ECS Fargate ARM64 migration was adopted only after validating resource efficiency under identical load.

details.problem: No capacity baseline (concurrent connections, requests/sec) for chat infrastructure shared across live games
details.solution: Analyzed commercial game chat solutions' rate limits and concurrency to define a capacity model for a single multi-tenant server frame
details.result: Set 6,000 CCU (sustained) / 18,000 RPS / 90,000 RPS burst targets, adopted into quarterly OKRs

details.problem: Redis Streams WAL hit a single-threaded write bottleneck at 6K msg/s (EngineCPU 99.9%, ack p95 767ms)
details.solution: Distributed the WAL stream across a 4-shard cluster and compacted entries into native fields (removing Lua serialization) — chose sharding because single-threaded Redis cannot scale writes vertically
details.result: Throughput 4,786→5,912 msg/s, message accept rate 99.39→99.99%, ack p95 767ms→6.6ms

details.problem: Latency and error-rate SLOs unverified under concurrent multi-tenant load
details.solution: Built a 5-tenant concurrent load-test environment and removed rejects via hot-path log removal and message scope keys
details.result: Achieved ack p95 42ms (target <100ms) and 0.04% error rate (target <0.1%) at 299K messages sustained over 5 minutes

details.problem: Unverified resource-efficiency and cost upside of x86 Fargate operation
details.solution: Migrated to ARM64 (Graviton) via multi-platform image builds and compared resource efficiency against x86 under 6,000 CCU load
details.result: Reduced CPU utilization 15% and memory 54% at identical load with neutral unit pricing — established operational cost-saving basis

details.problem: Fragmented ad platform management across Google Ads/Meta/TikTok
details.solution: Delivered unified campaign automation API for creation, deployment, modification, and retention metrics in a single platform

details.problem: Meta asset sync performance bottleneck
details.solution: Converted ORM single-row saves to bulk processing
details.result: Image sync reduced 72% (25.7s→7.1s), DB transactions reduced 95% (10~16s→0.3~0.5s)

details.problem: High BigQuery query costs for marketing data reads
details.solution: Adopted BigQuery Storage Read API with gRPC streaming-based high-performance data reading
details.result: Reduced BigQuery costs by 82% ($6.25→$1.1 per TB)

details.problem: Marketing query latency (18s) from 100+ column denormalized table
details.solution: Normalized table into main/time-series/prediction, tuned indexes + cursor pagination
details.result: Performance improved 97% (18s→0.5s)

details.problem: Large marketing-metrics archive backfill stalled at 63s Lambda runtime and 99.8% RDS CPU, ETA 15 hours
details.solution: Diagnosed the root cause as N+1 queries and a non-SARGable DATE() predicate (index miss) and removed both — chose a single 30-day batch fetch with in-memory latest-version dedup over per-row reads that were saturating RDS
details.result: Improved throughput 26x (9.3→247/min), Lambda runtime 63s→1.36s, RDS CPU 99.8%→5~7%

details.problem: Marketing RCP data was spreadsheet-only, and the BigQuery aggregation table combined multiple sources — blocking unified console queries
details.solution: Switched BigQuery to a single-source table, added Criteria-Result pattern field-metadata APIs, and built FE multi-select filters + TOTAL row aggregation
details.result: Embedded unified RCP queries into the console and replaced hardcoded currency/decimal display with BE metadata-driven formatting

projects.name: Internal Common Library System

details.problem: Concurrency conflicts in multi-instance environments

details.result: Applied distributed lock decorator consistently for multi-instance concurrency control

details.problem: Manual library upgrades taking 3 hours across 7 projects
details.solution: Added workflow_dispatch+matrix and changed-package CI tests on GitHub Packages
details.result: Reduced 7-project upgrade runtime 3h→15min

details.result: Cut CI time 61% (15m47s→6m06s); passed 81 suites/978 tests

details.problem: Game-server shared code split across 5 branches + one game's 17 sheet modules were 2+ years diverged from the published package

details.problem: Game-server cache logic was duplicated per project, increasing consistency and maintenance burden
details.solution: Packaged a hybrid strategy combining local LRU (hot-path latency) and distributed cache (cross-instance consistency) as a decorator-based AOP library — chose hybrid over pure-distributed (network round-trips) and pure-local (cross-instance inconsistency), splitting tag index and single-flight into separate modules per SRP
details.result: Released cache library v0.5.0 — 262 tests across 28 suites passing, 100% code-standard compliance

projects.name: In-Game Multi-Language Translation System

projects.techRationale: Materialized the responsibility boundary between AI translation and library-based derived conversion inside the code structure. Split the Detection → Processing (AI) → Conversion (library) pipeline into independent modules and secured concurrent request integrity with a 2-stage race guard plus pessimistic write lock

details.problem: Simplified Chinese was modeled inside the AI translation settings domain despite not being AI-supported, and settings storage/retrieval depended on the Traditional Chinese AI translation state — making independent toggling impossible without a breaking change
details.solution: Extracted the derived-conversion module from the AI translation module into 9 use cases with dedicated entity/repository/scheduler, and applied the global-inheritance pattern for effective settings

details.problem: Decoupling required a breaking API change
details.solution: Simultaneously deployed FE/BE/Gateway with role permission migration for zero-downtime transition
details.result: Completed the breaking API change without incident and cut effective-settings DB queries by 50% (4→2)

details.problem: The detect cron lacked version priority, delaying translation of the latest version; 30-second interval further slowed response
details.solution: Added version ID-based priority ordering to detect SQL, shortened the processing interval from 30s to 10s, and raised batch limit from 100 to 200
details.result: Eliminated latest-version translation lag; progress UI plus total-count caching improved user visibility

details.problem: Detect scheduler scanned 159 versions in one shot (3.27M-row full scan) — 60s login outages from RDS IOPS saturation
details.solution: Ported the per-version loop from the AI detect module, added distributed-lock timeout/recovery, and replaced the NOT EXISTS full scan with an indexed staged lookup
details.result: Cut query time 260x (full scan → 39ms indexed lookup), removed driving filesort, restored login latency

projects.name: Marketing Data Archiving & Custom Dashboard
projects.description: Built daily-snapshot archiving of marketing metrics (with immutability), a 4K-row custom dashboard, and alert observability
projects.techRationale: Archives must be immutable snapshots keyed by a reference-date cutoff rather than read-time state, so integrity was enforced with a stale-writer guard and tombstone states. The large grid uses visible-range lazy fetch with chunk caching instead of full loading.

details.problem: Displaying 4K-row marketing metrics in one dashboard caused scroll lag and cell-sync bugs
details.solution: Split BE (Raw SQL DISTINCT JOIN avoiding ORM hydration + in-memory cache) and FE (visible-row lazy fetch + 200-row chunks balancing network round-trips and render latency + per-pair caching) — rejected full loading due to response size and render cost
details.result: Displayed 3,341 of 4,458 rows mapped, stabilized response at 573ms cold / 221ms warm

details.problem: Sync paths used the latest snapshot instead of the reference-date cutoff, violating archive immutability (data contamination)
details.solution: Redesigned the usecase/repository to honor cutoff semantics, made the stale-writer guard transactional, and introduced tombstone states for sync
details.result: Rebuilt 15,333 live archives (zero contamination), validated 287,020 archive-date records

details.problem: A transient log-query stack (Loki) outage fired 16 marketing alerts at once, flooding ops channels
details.solution: After diagnosing the root cause, migrated all 16 alerts to a single analytics DB (ClickHouse) query, rewrote them via the dashboard API, and set a legacy log-stack decommission policy
details.result: Migrated 16/16 alerts (25 min), preventing alert-flood recurrence during log-stack outages
